question: Find the time for which compound interest of Rs. 331 was generated on principal of Rs. 1,000 at an annual interest rate of 10%.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Amount = Principal + CI = 1000 + 331 = 1331.

In Compound Interest, Ratio of Amount to Principal = 1331 / 1000 = (11 / 10)³

Since the rate is 10%, the yearly multiplying factor is (1 + 10/100) = 11/10.

The exponent directly gives the time period.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 1000

Compound Interest (CI) = Rs. 331

Rate (R) = 10% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R / 100)t

Amount (A) = P + CI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98895a9064bec0373dfea82f686857e41f508a8b712b4450f2a7eb45def5e493.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount (A) = 1000 + 331 = 1331

⇒ 1331 = 1000 × (1 + 10 / 100)t

⇒ 1331 / 1000 = (110 / 100)t

⇒ (11 / 10)³ = (11 / 10)t

Comparing the exponents on both sides:

⇒ t = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For a 10% annual rate, effective CI for 2 years is 21%, for 3 years is 33.1%, and for 4 years is 46.41%. Here, 33.1% of Rs. 1000 equates precisely to Rs. 331 directly confirming 3 years.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

D = P × (R / 100)². It helps solve standard 2-year gap exam questions directly.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

D = P × (R / 100)² × (3 + R / 100).

Rule of 72

To find the approximate time to double the principal at compound interest, use Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate.
